data.notes: 3,000 students start within 5 min. Autosave = 3,000 / 30 s = 100 req/s, mostly from ONE campus public IP.

data.label: Route 53 (exams.uni.edu)
data.notes: SPOF removed: global managed service (100% SLA).

data.label: CloudFront (CDN, HTTPS)
data.notes: SPOF removed: global edge network. PriceClass_200 includes India edges close to Bhutan.

data.label: AWS WAF (campus IP exempt from rate limit)

rules: ALLOW campus IP set (exempt from rate limit)  [A3 change C8]
rate limit 2,000 req / 5 min per IP for all other IPs

data.notes: BOTTLENECK FIXED (C8): A2 limit of 2,000 req/5 min per IP would block the exam hall (about 30,000 req/5 min from one shared campus IP).

data.label: S3 website bucket (React app)
data.notes: SPOF removed: S3 is regional and stores data across AZs.

data.label: Cognito (student / tutor / admin)
data.notes: SPOF removed: regional managed service across AZs.

data.label: Load balancer (AZ-a)
data.notes: SPOF removed: one ALB with nodes in both AZs; unhealthy targets removed after 2 x 10 s checks.

data.label: Load balancer (AZ-b)
data.notes: SPOF removed: one ALB with nodes in both AZs; unhealthy targets removed after 2 x 10 s checks.

data.label: NAT gateway A
data.notes: SPOF removed: one NAT per AZ, app subnet A routes only to its own NAT. Kept 2 (not 1) on purpose - a single NAT would cut off the healthy AZ (C13).

data.label: NAT gateway B
data.notes: SPOF removed: one NAT per AZ, app subnet B routes only to its own NAT. Kept 2 (not 1) on purpose - a single NAT would cut off the healthy AZ (C13).

data.label: API on ECS Fargate ARM64 (AZ-a)

customConfig.desiredCount: Normal: 1 per AZ (2 total). Exam days: 4 per AZ (8 total)
customConfig.autoScaling: 2-20 tasks; scheduled to min 8 ONLY on exam days [C3]; CPU target 60%
customConfig.pricing: Baseline 2 tasks covered by 1-year Compute Savings Plan; burst On-Demand [C4]
customConfig.dbConnections: psycopg_pool connection pool, 5 per worker (reused, not one per request) [C6]

data.notes: SPOF removed: tasks in both AZs; on exam days one AZ alone (4 tasks + auto scaling) carries the peak.

data.label: API on ECS Fargate ARM64 (AZ-b)

customConfig.desiredCount: Normal: 1 per AZ (2 total). Exam days: 4 per AZ (8 total)
customConfig.autoScaling: 2-20 tasks; scheduled to min 8 ONLY on exam days [C3]; CPU target 60%
customConfig.pricing: Baseline 2 tasks covered by 1-year Compute Savings Plan; burst On-Demand [C4]
customConfig.dbConnections: psycopg_pool connection pool, 5 per worker (reused, not one per request) [C6]

data.notes: SPOF removed: tasks in both AZs; on exam days one AZ alone (4 tasks + auto scaling) carries the peak.

data.label: RDS PostgreSQL PRIMARY (AZ-a) - RI
data.notes: SPOF removed by Multi-AZ standby (failover ~1-2 min, RPO ~0). BOTTLENECK: connections/CPU at peak - fixed by API connection pool (C6), proven in load test.

data.label: RDS PostgreSQL STANDBY (AZ-b)
data.notes: Multi-AZ standby: every write is copied here instantly; takes over automatically if AZ-a fails.

data.label: Internet gateway
data.notes: SPOF removed: horizontally scaled, redundant AWS-managed gateway.

data.label: S3 submissions (IA 90d, Deep Archive 1y, delete 5y)
data.notes: SPOF removed: regional, 11 nines durability. Files kept 5 years.

data.label: Lambda notifier

customConfig.trigger: S3 ObjectCreated event on exam-submissions (asynchronous invoke)
customConfig.resourcePolicy: allow s3.amazonaws.com to lambda:InvokeFunction (source: exam-submissions bucket)

data.notes: SPOF removed: regional; 2 async retries then DLQ.

data.label: Amazon SES (email)
data.notes: SPOF ACCEPTED: if SES is down only the email is delayed - the file is already safe in S3.

data.label: SQS marking-queue (+ dead-letter queue)
data.notes: SPOF removed: regional queue; DLQ after 3 failed tries.

data.label: Lambda MCQ auto-marker (max concurrency 5)

customConfig.vpc: attached to private app subnets A + B (to reach RDS)

data.notes: BOTTLENECK FIXED (C7): concurrency capped at 5 so a submit burst cannot exhaust DB connections; jobs wait in SQS.

data.label: IAM roles (Lambda + ECS)
data.notes: exam-notifier-role: ses:SendEmail (invoked by S3, no queue polling). exam-marker-role: same SQS actions on marking-queue. Both trust lambda.amazonaws.com.

data.label: KMS (encryption keys, 30-day deletion window)
data.notes: SPOF reduced (C12): 30-day window to cancel an accidental key deletion.

data.label: AWS Backup (daily 35 d + monthly 5 y)
data.notes: C9: 60 snapshots instead of 1,825 - same 5-year retention, far cheaper.

data.label: GitHub Actions (CI/CD)
data.notes: SPOF ACCEPTED: if GitHub is down we cannot deploy, but running tasks are not affected.

data.label: RDS Proxy (connection pooling, C6)
data.notes: BOTTLENECK FIXED (C6): API tasks and marker Lambda share a small pool of DB connections instead of one new TLS connection per request. Managed and multi-AZ; on RDS failover it holds client connections and reconnects to the new primary (faster recovery).

data.label: SNS alerts (email ops team)
data.notes: CloudWatch alarms publish here; ops team gets an email (5xx, latency, RDS CPU/connections, SQS backlog).

data.description: 1. Student opens exams.uni.edu; PUT /api/attempts/{id}/answers every 30 s
5. Load balancer sends it to a healthy API task
1. Browser uploads the 40 MB file straight to S3 (presigned URL)
2. S3 'file uploaded' event invokes the notifier Lambda (asynchronous)
3. Lambda calls SES SendEmail (email delivery is not simulated by the Lab)
Sign in, get a token with role = student
Before uploading: API gives a presigned URL (checks PDF/ZIP, <= 50 MB, deadline)
Multi-AZ: every write copied to the standby
Marker polls the queue, max 5 at once (C7)
3. CloudFront passes /api/* to WAF before the origin
4. WAF: campus IP set allowed, exempt from rate limit (C8) -> load balancer
AZ-a down: WAF-approved traffic goes to the load balancer in AZ-b
6. API borrows a pooled connection from RDS Proxy (C6)
6. API (AZ-b) uses the same RDS Proxy endpoint (C6)
7. Proxy sends the write to the RDS primary
After failover the standby is promoted; Proxy reconnects to it
Save MCQ scores through the proxy (max 5 Lambdas, C7)
